alignments.note: Verb beheld; the explicit pronoun takes its own I.

שִׁית לֵב is an idiom the ASV renders considered well; no English word writes either morpheme's own lexeme, so the phrase is indivisible, anchored on the first source token and headed on the lexical English anchor (rules 6 and 30).
The ASV writes no possessive for the suffix of לִבִּי (rules 18 and 22).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17).
No conjunction morpheme stands between the two clauses of the first colon, so the coordinating and answers to nothing (rule 14).
Likewise the and of the second colon: the Hebrew juxtaposes רָאִיתִי and לָקַחְתִּי asyndetically.

review_notes: considered well was left indivisible: neither considered nor well writes the lexeme of שִׁית or of לֵב, so rule 30's subtraction finds no morpheme owning a part.
The two supplied ands are marked separately because they stand between different pairs of clauses.
